claim_to_evidence.brent_price: documented by EIA: 104.47 USD/barrel on 7 September 2026
claim_to_evidence.hormuz_energy_significance: documented using official EIA chokepoint data already incorporated in the article's research record
claim_to_evidence.5_september_us_operations: attributed explicitly to the official CENTCOM account

temporal_check: The core sources used for the article were published no later than 7 September 2026; later information was not used to rewrite the 7 September account.
corroboration: EIA, IMO and CENTCOM cover distinct factual domains and are used without treating the CENTCOM account as independent corroboration.
contradiction: No contradiction identified for the Brent figure or IMO maritime-security figures. The CENTCOM account is explicitly identified as one-sided official attribution.
interpretation_risks: A rise in Brent cannot be attributed to a single cause solely from the cited official sources.
The article therefore avoids unsupported price forecasts and states that Ormuz was not established as formally closed.
unresolved_points: The duration and ultimate effect of the maritime disruption on energy flows remained uncertain on 7 September 2026.
The Iranian position on the CENTCOM account was not independently established in the cited primary sources.
human_approval: Historical article was already published after editorial remediation. This record documents the evidence used; it does not create a new publication approval.
